cards.q: What is the purpose of OSPF authentication?
cards.a: OSPF authentication validates the origin of Hello/LSA packets to stop rogue routers or injected LSAs from poisoning the domain. OSPFv2 supports null (none), plaintext, and MD5/SHA message-digest authentication carried in the header. OSPFv3 has no OSPF-level auth and relies on IPv6 AH/ESP (IPsec). Adjacencies fail if the auth method or key mismatches.

cards.q: What are the OSPFv2 authentication types and their values?
cards.a: Null (type 0, none, default), Plaintext/Simple (type 1, weak, sent in clear), MD5/HMAC-SHA (type 2, strong digest, key not in packet, recommended), and Cryptographic SHA-256+ (type 2+, strongest, newer IOS/XE). Type 2 message-digest is the correct security answer on the exam.

cards.q: At what levels can OSPFv2 authentication be configured?
cards.a: Per-interface with ip ospf authentication message-digest plus a key, per-area with area N authentication message-digest (applies to all interfaces in the area), and per-virtual-link with area N virtual-link X authentication message-digest.

cards.q: Describe the OSPF MD5 digest process.
cards.a: 1. Each OSPF packet gets a key ID and cryptographic sequence number in its header. 2. A digest is computed over the packet with the shared key. 3. The receiver verifies the digest and sequence, rejecting replay or reforged packets.

cards.q: How does OSPFv3 authentication differ from OSPFv2?
cards.a: OSPFv2 uses MD5/SHA in the header for in-band authentication. OSPFv3 has no native authentication and relies on IPv6 AH/ESP or IPsec. On the exam, OSPFv3 authentication answers point to IPsec/AH, not OSPF keys.

cards.q: What happens when OSPF authentication fails?
cards.a: On an auth mismatch, the neighbor gets stuck in INIT (hellos dropped) and never reaches 2-Way. A key or type mismatch on both ends causes silence, no adjacency, and logged errors.

cards.q: How do you rotate OSPF authentication keys without breaking adjacency?
cards.a: Use the key ID and sequence number, keeping multiple keys valid during the transition. Add the new key first and keep both briefly before removing the old one.

cards.q: What command shows the OSPF authentication type on an interface?
cards.a: show ip ospf interface Gi0/1 shows the auth type. Also show ip ospf neighbor and show ip ospf with the Authentication filter are useful.

cards.q: Which OSPFv2 authentication type is the strong/recommended one?
cards.a: Type 2 (message-digest / MD5/HMAC-SHA) is the strong authentication. Plaintext Type 1 is legacy and weak because it is sent in clear.

cards.q: What neighbor state indicates an OSPF authentication mismatch?
cards.a: The neighbor is stuck in INIT, because authenticated Hellos are dropped and never reach 2-Way.

cards.q: Does a virtual link need its own OSPF authentication configuration?
cards.a: Yes. Virtual links need their own authentication on the virtual-link line, e.g. area 2 virtual-link 2.2.2.2 authentication message-digest with a message-digest-key.
OSPFv3 has no native authentication and relies on IPv6 AH/ESP or IPsec. It does not use OSPFv2-style keys.

cards.q: Summarize the OSPF authentication quick-review facts.
cards.a: Null is type 0 (default), plaintext type 1 (weak), MD5/HMAC-SHA type 2 (recommended), OSPFv3 uses IPsec AH/ESP, config levels are interface/area/virtual-link, mismatch causes neighbor stuck in INIT, rotation uses key ID and sequence, show with show ip ospf interface, and virtual links need auth on the virtual-link line.
